where: Section 1, 'Two assumptions make the method work'
problem: The chapter states as a required assumption that n(x) is odd AND memoryless (output depends only on the present input). But Section 2 and the exam traps then treat backlash, whose output depends on the direction of past motion, and whose describing function is complex. A student will think backlash cannot be analysed by this method, contradicting the rest of the chapter.
fix: Say: 'The nonlinearity must be odd, n(−x)=−n(x), and time-invariant. For single-valued nonlinearities such as saturation and an ideal relay, it is also memoryless. Memory-type nonlinearities such as backlash and relays with hysteresis break the memoryless condition: their describing function is derived over one full input period, is complex, and depends on the hysteresis width as well as on A.'

problem: 'A small change in A must move the operating point toward the stable side' is circular and does not tell the student how to do the check. The stable side is exactly what the check is supposed to decide.
fix: Give the usable rule: 'For a single intersection, the limit cycle is stable if, as A increases through the intersection, the point on the −1/N locus crosses from inside the G(jω) locus to outside. Also check the ω direction along G(jω). Unstable crossings do not produce a sustained oscillation.'

problem: The lead defines N(A) as 'the amplitude of the fundamental output divided by A', a real number, while Section 1 defines it as the complex ratio of phasors Y1/A. The quiz answer repeats the real-word 'amplitude' and then adds that it may be complex. The two statements sit uneasily together.
fix: Use one definition everywhere: 'N(A) = Y1/A is the complex ratio of the fundamental output phasor Y1 to the input phasor A; its magnitude is the output-to-input fundamental amplitude ratio and its angle is the fundamental phase shift. N(A) is real when the nonlinearity causes no phase shift, e.g. saturation and an ideal relay.'

problem: The pointer 'See 7.4 Limit cycles' is plain text, so the student cannot jump to it on a phone, unlike other chapter cross-references in the series.
fix: Make it a chapter link: 'See 7.4 Limit cycles for the exact definition of an isolated closed path.'
